schema.selection: A card applies when every key in its `applies` block passes. Absent key means no constraint. Among applying cards, highest `priority` wins; ties break on array order, earliest first. See pickCard/cardApplies in web/app.js.

applies_keys.down: list of ints, matches the current down
applies_keys.min_pass_rate: float, the rate the card would print must be >= this
applies_keys.max_pass_rate: float, the rate the card would print must be <= this
applies_keys.period: list of ints, 1-4 plus 5+ for overtime
applies_keys.max_clock_seconds: int, seconds left in the period must be <= this, and a null clock fails the gate
applies_keys.min_score_diff: int, offense score minus defense score, pre-snap, must be >= this

placeholders.{pass_rate}: round(100 * printed rate), integer, no percent sign in the value
placeholders.{yards_to_goal}: yards to the opponent end zone, integer

schema.no_team_placeholder: There is no {team} placeholder and there must not be one. `fill` in app.js does not substitute it, and CFB team names run one to three words, which would make the 25 word cap unenforceable. The team name is carried by the source chip app.js draws under the card, on exactly the snaps `can_attribute` allows and never on the rest.
schema.attribution: Two registers, chosen by the exported `can_attribute` flag alone, per CONTRACT.md. `tendency` is the attributed line and says 'They', with the team named in the chip beside it. `tendency_low` is the unattributed line and says 'Offenses', with the chip reading 'All offenses'. Measured over every eligible snap in the parquet, 46.5% of NFL and 52.4% of CFB snaps may name the team and the rest must say offenses. Neither line hedges a number it prints: no 'usually', no 'about', no 'roughly' next to a percentage.
schema.prints_number: True when the card's tendency lines carry {pass_rate} or {run_rate}. False cards say something qualitative that is true of the situation the card actually gates on. Eight cards are false, for three reasons given below. On a false card the source chip is telling the reader nothing, because no number came from that team; app.js uses the general source label for these cards.
schema.why_some_cards_print_no_number: The tendency tables are keyed on down, distance band and field zone only. A card that also gates on clock or score prints a number averaged over every clock and every score, which was measured 30 to 35 points wrong on the three late-game cards. Those three carry a qualitative line verified against their own gate instead. Separately, the NFL table has no league baseline and no team row for d1_short_own_deep, d1_short_own, d1_short_mid or d1_short_opp, so no card that can fire on first-and-short outside the red zone is allowed to print a number. Third, the tables count throws and runs, so a card about whether a team kicks at all cannot read its answer out of them; the four fourth-down cards state a kick frequency verified directly against the parquet over their own gate, or in the case of d4_kick_range_edge state none, because that band splits 82% kicks in the NFL against 55% in college and no single sentence is true of both.
schema.ask: An optional prediction before the next play is revealed. Prediction accuracy does not establish concept recognition or a learning effect in this app. `kind` selects the answer buttons from ASK_KINDS in app.js and must be one of passrun, gokick, kickrunpass, sticks; `q` overrides the default question; `opts` mirrors what app.js renders and is here so the file is readable on its own; `resolve` says how the reader can tell what the right answer was. `ask_priority` rations the mechanic: app.js asks sooner on high numbers and later on low ones. Simulated over the whole parquet through app.js's own askEligible, this file asks once per 6.6 plays in both leagues, counted over every snap the app sees, and never twice running.
schema.exposure: Use `watch` with definitions by default. Use `watch_short` only when the reader enables Shorter hints. The ledger records exposure, not knowledge; prediction accuracy never changes the copy register.
schema.assembly: Three lines: situation, tendency, watch. Combined word count is capped at 25 and every variant pairing in this file is at or under it.
schema.example_fill: Not for rendering. A real snap from data/plays_{nfl,cfb}.parquet that selects this card, with the number app.js would print for it read out of the shipped tendency table, and the assembled word count. Regenerated whenever the tables are rebuilt.

concepts.blitz: extra defenders running at the quarterback instead of covering
concepts.box: the defenders crowded near where the ball sits
concepts.center: the player in the middle of the offensive line who snaps the ball
concepts.clock_stops: the clock stops out of bounds and on missed passes
concepts.cushion: the space a defender leaves in front of a receiver
concepts.field_goal: a kick between the tall posts, worth three points
concepts.line_of_scrimmage: the line across the field where the ball sits
concepts.linebacker: a defender in the second row, behind the big men
concepts.motion: a player jogging sideways behind the line before the snap
concepts.offensive_line: the five blockers lined up in front of the quarterback
concepts.play_action: the quarterback fakes giving the ball away, then throws
concepts.pocket: the space the blockers build around the quarterback
concepts.punt: a kick that hands the ball to the other team
concepts.quarterback: the player who usually takes the snap, then hands off, throws, or runs
concepts.receiver: a player whose job is to run out and catch
concepts.red_zone: inside the opponent's twenty yard line
concepts.returner: the player waiting to catch a kick and run it back
concepts.safety: the deepest defender, playing behind everyone else
concepts.slot: a receiver lined up inside the widest one
concepts.snap: the moment the ball is passed back to start play
concepts.sticks: the first-down marker, drawn on TV as a yellow line
concepts.zone_coverage: each defender guards an area, not a specific man

prime.tendency: They run here {run_rate}% of the time.
prime.tendency_low: Offenses run here {run_rate}% of the time.
prime.watch: Watch the line of scrimmage, where the ball sits. How crowded is it?
prime.watch_short: Watch how packed the line of scrimmage is.

ask.resolve: Watch the quarterback's hands. If the ball went to a runner, you called run right.

cards.explain_hint: Near the goal line, there is less room for receivers to work. Watch whether extra blockers help open a running lane.

prime.tendency: Trailing late, they mostly throw.
prime.tendency_low: Trailing late, offenses mostly throw.
prime.watch: Find the safeties, the deepest defenders. How far back are they?
prime.watch_short: Watch how deep the safeties start.

ask.q: Will a pass get past the yellow line?
ask.resolve: The yellow line settles it. A catch in front of the line leaves them still short.

cards.explain_hint: A team trailing late needs yards quickly. Deep defenders can leave room for short catches, but those catches still use time.

prime.tendency: Leading late, they mostly run.
prime.tendency_low: Leading late, offenses mostly run.
prime.watch: Watch the box, the defenders crowded near the ball.
prime.watch_short: Watch how crowded the box is.

ask.q: With that many defenders near the ball, run or throw?
ask.resolve: If the box was crowded and they ran anyway, the clock mattered more than the picture.

cards.explain_hint: Running can keep the clock moving. With a late lead, using time may matter more than gaining a lot of yards.

prime.tendency: They throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.tendency_low: Offenses throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.watch: Watch the pocket, the space the blockers build around the quarterback.
prime.watch_short: Watch how much room the pocket gives the quarterback.

ask.resolve: If he dropped straight back and the pocket held, it was a throw all along.

cards.explain_hint: Watch whether the blockers give the quarterback room to throw. A sack this close to his own end zone can be especially costly.

prime.tendency: They throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.tendency_low: Offenses throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.watch: A blitz is extra rushers. Watch who creeps toward the line late.
prime.watch_short: Watch for extra defenders moving toward the line.

ask.q: Will a pass get past the yellow line?
ask.resolve: The yellow line settles it. Note how fast the ball came out once the rushers arrived.

cards.explain_hint: If extra defenders rush, fewer are available to cover receivers. The quarterback may need to release the ball quickly.

prime.tendency: They throw {pass_rate}% when they go for it.
prime.tendency_low: Offenses throw {pass_rate}% when they go for it.
prime.watch: Watch who lines up behind the center, the player who hands the ball back.
prime.watch_short: Watch who stands behind the center.

ask.resolve: A kicker swings his leg. A quarterback takes it and turns. You could see which was back there.

cards.explain_hint: With only a few yards to gain, going for it can keep the drive alive. Failing gives the other team the ball at that spot.

prime.tendency: Three times in four, they punt.
prime.tendency_low: Three times in four, offenses punt.
prime.watch: A punt hands the ball over. Watch the punter standing fifteen yards back.
prime.watch_short: Watch whether the punter is standing back there.

ask.resolve: If the punter was standing fifteen yards back, it was always going to be a kick.

cards.explain_hint: A failed fourth-down try here gives the opponent a short field. A punt can move the ball farther from the end zone you are defending.

prime.tendency: They kick from here most of the time.
prime.tendency_low: Offenses kick from here most of the time.
prime.watch: A field goal is a kick between the posts. Watch the holder kneel.
prime.watch_short: Watch the field goal holder kneel down.

ask.resolve: If a man knelt down to hold the ball, the field goal team was on the field.

cards.explain_hint: A field goal offers three points. Going for a first down keeps a touchdown possible, but risks coming away with no points.

prime.tendency: A long kick or a fourth-down try.
prime.tendency_low: A long kick or a fourth-down try.
prime.watch: Watch whether the kicking team comes on.
prime.watch_short: Watch which players run on.

ask.resolve: The group that ran on settled this before the ball ever moved.

cards.explain_hint: This is a long field-goal attempt. The kicker, weather, score, and yards needed all matter to the decision.

prime.tendency: Nine times in ten, they punt.
prime.tendency_low: Nine times in ten, offenses punt.
prime.watch: A punt hands the ball over. Watch the returner waiting far away to catch it.
prime.watch_short: Watch the returner set up far away for the punt.

ask.resolve: If one player was standing alone forty yards away, the kick was coming.

cards.explain_hint: A punt gives up possession to move the opponent farther back. Watch where the returner catches it and how far he gets.

prime.tendency: They throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.tendency_low: Offenses throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.watch: Watch the offensive line, the five blockers up front.
prime.watch_short: Watch the offensive line up front.

ask.q: Run or throw for the first down?
ask.resolve: If the line fired forward off the ball, that was the run you called.

cards.explain_hint: On a short-yardage run, watch whether the blockers move defenders back or open a gap. A small opening can be enough.

prime.tendency: They throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.tendency_low: Offenses throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.watch: Watch where defenders set up against the sticks, the yellow first-down line.
prime.watch_short: Watch who sets up short of the sticks.

ask.q: Will a pass get past the yellow line?
ask.resolve: The yellow line settles it. What counts is where he was stopped, not where he caught it.

cards.explain_hint: Compare where the catch happens with the first-down line. A short catch still needs room to run before it becomes a first down.

prime.tendency: They throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.tendency_low: Offenses throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.watch: Find the safeties, the deepest defenders, and the sticks, the yellow first-down line.
prime.watch_short: Compare the safeties with the sticks.

ask.q: Will a pass get past the yellow line?
ask.resolve: The yellow line settles it. Short of it on third down means the punt team comes on.

cards.explain_hint: On third and long, a defense may allow a short catch and rely on the tackle. Watch how much space remains after the catch.

prime.tendency: Down or tied late, they mostly throw.
prime.tendency_low: Down or tied late, offenses mostly throw.
prime.watch: Watch the sideline. Getting out of bounds can stop the clock.
prime.watch_short: Watch whether the ball carrier gets out of bounds.

ask.q: Will a pass get past the yellow line?
ask.resolve: The yellow line settles it. Past the line is a new first down and the chains move.

cards.explain_hint: Watch where the play ends. Getting out of bounds or throwing an incomplete pass can preserve time for the next play.

prime.tendency: They throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.tendency_low: Offenses throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.watch: Watch the slot, the receiver just inside the widest one.
prime.watch_short: Watch the slot in the red zone.

ask.q: Run or throw near the end zone?
ask.resolve: If the ball went to the slot on a short route, your read on that inside spot was right.

cards.explain_hint: Near the end zone, receivers have less room to run deep. Watch how the inside receiver finds space between defenders.

prime.tendency: They run here {run_rate}% of the time.
prime.tendency_low: Offenses run here {run_rate}% of the time.
prime.watch: Watch whether the safeties, the deepest defenders, move toward the line.
prime.watch_short: Watch whether the safeties move toward the line.

ask.resolve: If the safeties came down and the throw went over the top, the creep gave it away.

cards.explain_hint: With only a few yards needed, the offense can risk a longer throw. Watch whether defenders step forward expecting a run.

prime.tendency: They throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.tendency_low: Offenses throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.watch: Watch for motion, a player jogging sideways before the snap.
prime.watch_short: Watch for a player moving sideways before the snap.

ask.resolve: The quarterback's hands settle it. A handoff is a run, dropping back is a throw.

cards.explain_hint: A defender following a receiver across the field can suggest man coverage: one defender assigned to one receiver. It is a clue, since defenses can disguise assignments.

prime.tendency: They throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.tendency_low: Offenses throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.watch: Watch the linebackers behind the front line. In zone coverage, they guard areas.
prime.watch_short: Watch whether the linebackers guard areas in zone coverage.

ask.resolve: The quarterback's hands settle it. Then check whether the linebackers had backed off.

cards.explain_hint: In zone coverage, defenders cover areas of the field. Watch how they react when a receiver enters or leaves their area.

prime.tendency: No tendency available for this situation.
prime.tendency_low: No tendency available for this situation.
prime.watch: Watch the box, the defenders crowded near the ball.
prime.watch_short: Watch how crowded the box is.

ask.resolve: A crowded box that still gave up a run tells you the picture is only ever a hint.

cards.explain_hint: There are only a few yards to gain for a new first down. Watch how many defenders line up near the ball.

prime.tendency: They run here {run_rate}% of the time.
prime.tendency_low: Offenses run here {run_rate}% of the time.
prime.watch: Watch for a fake handoff before a throw. That is play action.
prime.watch_short: Watch for a play-action fake to the runner.

ask.q: Will they hand it off or throw?
ask.resolve: If he faked to the runner and kept the ball, it was a throw all along.

cards.explain_hint: A fake handoff can draw defenders toward the runner and open space behind them. Watch whether anyone reacts to the fake.

prime.tendency: They throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.tendency_low: Offenses throw here {pass_rate}% of the time.
prime.watch: Watch the cushion, the space a defender leaves in front of a receiver.
prime.watch_short: Watch the cushion on the receivers.

ask.resolve: If the cushion was big and the throw went underneath it, your read was the right one.

cards.explain_hint: Space in front of a receiver can make a short throw easier. Watch how quickly the defender closes that space after the snap.

prime.tendency: They run here {run_rate}% of the time.
prime.tendency_low: Offenses run here {run_rate}% of the time.
prime.watch: Count the defenders in the box, the area near the ball.
prime.watch_short: Count the defenders in the box.

ask.resolve: The quarterback's hands settle it. Then look back at the box and see whether it matched.

cards.explain_hint: Fewer defenders near the ball can leave more room to run. Extra defenders there may leave space for a throw elsewhere.
